questions.q: In Tableau's order of operations, where do FIXED LOD expressions get computed relative to dimension filters?
options: Before dimension filters — FIXED sees data that has only passed through extract, data source, and context filters
After dimension filters — FIXED always reflects every regular filter on the view
At the same time as dimension filters, in no particular order
After table calculation filters, last in the whole pipeline
questions.explain: FIXED is computed after extract/data source/context filters, but before ordinary dimension filters — which is exactly why a regular dimension filter doesn't change a FIXED result.

questions.q: Where do INCLUDE and EXCLUDE LOD expressions get computed relative to dimension filters?
options: After dimension filters — so they do reflect a regular filter's effect
Before dimension filters, exactly like FIXED
Before context filters
They are never affected by any filter, under any circumstances
questions.explain: INCLUDE and EXCLUDE are computed after ordinary dimension filters have already removed rows, so they reflect the filtered data — unlike FIXED.

questions.q: How do you make a regular filter run before a FIXED calculation computes?
options: Right-click the filter pill and select Add to Context, promoting it to a context filter
Rewrite the filter as a table calculation filter
Swap FIXED for INCLUDE in the calculation
There is no way — FIXED can never be affected by any filter
questions.explain: Promoting a filter to context moves it to stage 3 of the order of operations, before FIXED (stage 4) computes.

questions.q: A customer has orders in both East and West. With Region = West set as a REGULAR filter, what does { FIXED [Customer Name] : SUM([Sales]) } show for that customer?
options: Their total sales across East + West combined, unchanged by the regular filter
Only their West sales, because all filters always apply first
Zero, because the customer also has East sales
An error, since FIXED can't be combined with any filter
questions.explain: A regular dimension filter runs after FIXED has already computed, so FIXED still returns the customer's full East+West total — this only changes once Region is promoted to a context filter.

questions.q: What is the correct high-level order: extract filters, data source filters, context filters, dimension filters, measure filters, table calculation filters — where do FIXED and INCLUDE/EXCLUDE fit in?
options: FIXED computes right after context filters (before dimension filters); INCLUDE/EXCLUDE compute right after dimension filters (before measure filters)
Both FIXED and INCLUDE/EXCLUDE compute before extract filters
FIXED computes after measure filters; INCLUDE/EXCLUDE compute before extract filters
Both FIXED and INCLUDE/EXCLUDE compute after table calculation filters, at the very end
questions.explain: The full pipeline is: extract → data source → context → FIXED → dimension → INCLUDE/EXCLUDE → measure → table calculation filters. This ordering is the single explanation for most LOD-and-filter surprises.
